title: Create ability to register handling of pcapng custom block enterprise numbers
description: Convert current Netflix block to use as an example.

notes.body:
This is a draft for a few reasons:

1. Wiretap needs a way to initialize/cleanup "file types" (unsure what you'd call the modules within the library). Adding to open_info_base doesn't seem like the right way to go, because this isn't about the file itself, but adding flexibility to the file data (mostly pcapng). So suggestions welcome.
2. Function/Structure/Variable naming - Everything in pcapng seems to be a "block". Are there "blocks within blocks" but both are labelled as just "blocks"? Trying to find the right names for the hooks I want to add to give more plugin capability
3. There look to be several maps/tables that could be added to the pcapng module to maximize plugin flexibility. Is now the time to create them? I think the maps/tables should be created with "pcapng module initialization" (which should come out of item 1 above

I added register_pcapng_local_block_dissector() a while back.  I prefer the way this function works though, because:
- the user of it doesn't need to know or create the block type (cuustom_block_handler)
- a deep copy is taken of the args passed in, whereas for the local dissector function it had to persist, so in the example (and my private dissectors), I made the blocks static when they were registered, which is a bug waiting to happen

I'd like to change it to be more like this.  Nothing was added under doc, I wonder if anyone would notice...

I started this patch based off of register_pcapng_option_handler(), as it seemed to make sense to pass in the function pointers as arguments, but I have no problem switching to passing in a structure (because the number of function pointers needed seems to have grown).

But you seem to be presenting a different problem - register_pcapng_local_block_dissector() is for _file_ dissection and I'm looking for APIs for the wiretap label.  Is there any reason your private dissectors don't need wiretap functionality too?

> But you seem to be presenting a different problem - register_pcapng_local_block_dissector() is for _file_ dissection and I'm looking for APIs for the wiretap label. Is there any reason your private dissectors don't need wiretap functionality too?

There's no inherent need - yes, it means there are two separate pieces of code that understand the structure of a particular capture file format, but they're doing different things with that structure (extracting the data for the Wireshark/TShark code to process as opposed to parsing the raw binary file for the Fileshark/TFShark part of the code).

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19781/diffs?diff_id=1353124265&start_sha=c40cbc812c7414e07dd82d368760e7bedb0513aa#247de00fe9a1f9373f0ffe8c59cfc1d73f691691_2961_2920)

To be precise, it deserves a home in a register routine in wiretap/pcapng-netflix-custom.c.  That routine is, as of 8c708992e7820fffad60b79632581e0e548d80ff, called `void register_nflx_custom(void)`; it's at the bottom of that file that makes the call. wiretap/pcapng-netflix-custom.c is now in `WIRETAP_C_MODULE_FILES` in wiretap/CMakeLists.txt, so that it's one of the files scanned for a register routine.

The eventual goal of this exercise is to arrange that support for custom blocks and options can be added *without* changing any files other than CMakeLists.txt files to add new source files.
I like the home you gave it and I'll incorporate that into this MR.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19781/diffs?diff_id=1353124265&start_sha=c40cbc812c7414e07dd82d368760e7bedb0513aa#994e3719ff20d5a5a693ca2f070272a2aeca4f44_494_491)

> 1. Wiretap needs a way to initialize/cleanup "file types" (unsure what you'd call the modules within the library). Adding to open_info_base doesn't seem like the right way to go, because this isn't about the file itself, but adding flexibility to the file data (mostly pcapng). So suggestions welcome.

The "file type" you're dealing with is pcapng; there's no need to do anything to wiretap/file_access.c here.

> 2. Function/Structure/Variable naming - Everything in pcapng seems to be a "block".

Yes. See [section 3 "General File Structure" of the pcapng specification](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng#name-general-file-structure).

> Are there "blocks within blocks"

Some blocks contain what might be considered "sub-blocks", e.g. the records in a [Name Resolution Block](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng#name-name-resolution-block). The other block types don't.

> but both are labelled as just "blocks"?

No, the "sub-blocks" in an NRB are called "records".

3. There look to be several maps/tables that could be added to the pcapng module to maximize plugin flexibility. Is now the time to create them?

Yes.

> I think the maps/tables should be created with "pcapng module initialization" (which should come out of item 1 above

Initialization is handled by register functions in source files; files in the `WIRETAP_C_MODULE_FILES` macro in wiretap/CMakeLists.txt are scanned to see if they define a register routine, and entries for all the register routines are put into a wtap_modules.c file in the `wiretap` subdirectory of the directory in which the build is put (vague phrasing because it's different on UN\*Xes and Windows), so that they all get called at startup time.

The startup process initializes pcap and pcapng first, for various reasons that are unlikely to change, especially given that you want pcapng initialized before any pcap modules.

So the "design" is that custom (pcapng) block handling can be handled in its own module as long as the file provides a register_XXX() function that will include the call to register handling of enterprise number or other "hooks" yet to be added.  i.e. register_nflx_custom() will call register_pcapng_custom_block_enterprise_handler() and register_sysdig() could call register_pcapng_block_type() (if either of those existed).

This would work for "built in" and "plugin".  I definitely missed this "registration through CMake" when I started this patch, so thank you.

Does "registration" count as "initialization"?  After reading this I wanted to add the new hash tables within register_pcapng(), but there isn't a corresponding "cleanup".  Should I be making changes to tools\\make-regs.py for such a design?  Should register_pcapng() and register_pcap() be renamed to something like pcapng_file_init(), so it can have a corresponding pcapng_file_cleanup() (and not need any CMake/python magic). I don't expect the other file formats to need the flexibility (i.e. hooks for extensions to their file formats), but trying to make it as generic as possible from the start.

> Does "registration" count as "initialization"?

Until we need a reason not to have the registration routine do initialization, yes.

> After reading this I wanted to add the new hash tables within register_pcapng(), but there isn't a corresponding "cleanup".

We don't currently have a mechanism for unregistering wiretap modules. For that matter, the places where we support unregistration of that sort is there only for Lua plugins - no compiled plugins support it.

And this is not a place where we unallocate things at exit time (process termination releases all that memory).

> Should register_pcapng() and register_pcap() be renamed to something like pcapng_file_init(), so it can have a corresponding pcapng_file_cleanup() (and not need any CMake/python magic).

No, because they perform the same registration process that the other modules' registration routines do.

There's only a small amount of CMake magic (`WIRETAP_C_MODULE_FILES` vs. `WIRETAP_NONGENERATED_C_FILES`) and no tools/make_regs.py magi for this.

> I don't expect the other file formats to need the flexibility (i.e. hooks for extensions to their file formats),

Only if they have pcapng-style extensability, which I don't think any of them edo.
